videos.title: Every Word Shaytan Speaks in the Quran, Explained
videos.description:
Iblis speaks in the Quran more than most people realise — and he never once denies that Allah exists. This goes through what he actually says, in Arabic, passage by passage.

What this covers:
• Every passage where Iblis or Shaytan is quoted directly
• What his refusal actually was, in the Arabic — and why it was not disbelief in God's existence
• The exact request he makes, and what Allah grants him
• Where the mufassirun differ on his nature and his reach

Every verse is cited by surah and ayah. The Arabic on screen is set from a verified mushaf. Where scholars disagree, the disagreement is named rather than smoothed over.

This channel explains; it issues no ruling.

📖 Tafsir in English, verse by verse — for people with no Arabic and no background.
New study every week.

videos.title: Sabr Doesn't Mean Patience: What the Arabic Actually Says
videos.description:
"Sabr" gets translated as patience, and patience sounds like waiting. The Arabic root says something closer to holding a grip — and that changes every verse it appears in.

What this covers:
• The root of sabr and what it originally described
• Why "patience" is a lossy translation, and what the English drops
• How the meaning reads differently across the verses that command it
• What sabr asks of you that waiting does not

Every verse is cited by surah and ayah. The Arabic on screen is set from a verified mushaf.

videos.title: Surah Al-Qalam: The Garden Story Most People Read Wrong
videos.description:

• The full narrative in Surah Al-Qalam, verse by verse
• What the "righteous" brother actually said, and when he said it

videos.title: Huzn: The Sadness the Quran Never Condemns
videos.description:
The Quran uses "huzn" for sadness — and it is never once commanded against as a sin. Prophets feel it. The Arabic is specific about what it is and what it is not.

What this covers:
• What huzn means at the root, and how it differs from despair
• Where the Quran attributes huzn to prophets
• The difference between being told not to grieve and being told grief is wrong
• What the English translation flattens

videos.title: Every Arabic Word for Time in the Quran Explained (Ajal and Waqt)
videos.description:
The Quran does not use one word for time. It uses several, and they are not interchangeable — ajal is not waqt, and neither is what English means by "time".

What this covers:
• Ajal: a fixed term with an endpoint, and where it is used
• Waqt: an appointed moment, and how it differs
• The other time-words the translations collapse into one
• What is lost when every one of them becomes "time"

Every verse is cited by surah and ayah. The Arabic on screen is set from a verified mushaf.

videos.title: Surah Ar-Ra'd 28 Explained: The Half of the Verse Nobody Quotes
videos.description:
"Hearts find rest in the remembrance of Allah" is one of the most quoted verses in the Quran. It is almost always quoted at half length, and the Arabic word at its centre does not mean rest.

What this covers:
• Tuma'ninah: what the word actually describes, and why "peace" misses it
• The half of Ar-Ra'd 28 that gets cut off, and what it adds
• How the full verse reads against the partial one
• Where the mufassirun place the emphasis

videos.title: Surah Al-Isra 23: Honoring Parents Is Decreed, Not Requested
videos.description:
Al-Isra 23 does not ask you to honour your parents. The verb is qada — decreed — and it sits in the same breath as the command to worship none but Allah.

What this covers:
• Qada: what the verb carries that "commanded" or "asked" does not
• Why the instruction is placed directly beside tawhid
• What ihsan means here, beyond obedience
• The specific limits the passage sets, word by word
